text:
incident-bot: ALERT: hosted-api queue depth (us-east-1) > 12k requests for 3m, p99 gen latency > 18s, visible 504s. severity: high. paging @oncall_ava :rotating_light:

oncall_ava: I’m on it. seeing huge backlog on main router. dashboards show GPU pool util 100% and the autoscaler failing to create instances (quota errors). linking logs below.

sre-liam: can you paste the error from provisioner? might be rate-limit or quota.

oncall_ava: logs from provisioner: ```
2026-03-15T02:01:04Z ERROR provisioner: create_instance failed: QuotaExceeded: quota for g4dn in eu-west-1 reached
request id: abc-123
status: 403 rate_limited=false
```

infra-maya: interesting — quotaExceeded in eu-west-1 while metric is us-east-1? our multi-region placement tries eu for cheap spot but it tripped quota guardrails and the provisioner loop retried and hit cloud API rate limits. previous autoscale attempts: ```retries: 5 backoff: 8s last_err: QuotaExceeded```

runtime-igor: because the provisioner loop stalls, the scheduler can't bind new jobs to other pools fast enough. KV cache pressure spikes and token-shed starts firing which leads to 504s. p95 jumped from 120ms -> 1.6s then p99 -> 18s in ~6m.

sre-liam: mitigation plan proposal: 1) temporarily enable cross-tenant throttling (soft cap per org) 2) route high-volume tenants to dedicated fallback pool (if they have one) 3) scale up a small CPU fallback fleet for best-effort gen to reduce total queue depth 4) open quota request with cloud + escalate support.

support-jade: customers complaining of timeouts, major customer EastCorp (CS rep) reporting errors on their production traffic. tagging cs-eastcorp.

cs-eastcorp: we’re seeing 20% of calls return 504s since 01:58 UTC, customer impact: chatbots go silent -> revenue-affecting. need ETA.

product-sam: priorities: keep paying customers online. happy with degraded quality if latency is bounded. can we route EastCorp to a reserved dedicated pool?

oncall_ava: actioning now: 1) adding a temporary route rule to send EastCorp traffic -> dedicated-pool-3 (if capacity) 2) enabling per-org throttle at 30 rps 3) spin up cpu-fallback nodes with lower-cost models. executing commands.

sre-liam: commands you ran?

oncall_ava: ```bash
# add rules to router
redwoodctl route create --match org:eastcorp --pool dedicated-pool-3 --priority 100 --reason "incident 1811112223"
# enable throttling globally for free-tier
redwoodctl config update --path /limits/free_tier/rps --value 30
# provision cpu fallback
provisioner start --region us-east-1 --flavor c5.large --count 8 --image runtime-fallback:v2
```

infra-maya: router accepted rule, but dedicated-pool-3 has only 120 tokens free -> will take a few mins to drain. cpu-fallback provisioner returns: `create_instances: accepted 8, pending allocation` (no quota errors). good sign.

runtime-igor: I’m enabling prefix/KV cache aggressive eviction to free hot slots and enabling soft-batching size -> reduces per-request GPU pressure. ETA 90s to be effective.

support-jade: EastCorp confirm they see partial restoration on a few calls now but still elevated latencies. they want a status message to customers.

cs-eastcorp: partial restore observed, p95 about 2.4s now, p99 ~9s. still bad but improved vs 18s. mid-sized customers also report intermittent 504s.

sre-liam: next steps: 1) keep throttles in place 2) keep cpu-fallback running, promote to accept non-LLM-heavy routes (embeddings offloaded) 3) open cloud quota case and request urgent quota bump for g4dn in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 4) run temporary manual scale: increase dedicated-pool-3 by +4 gpus if cloud quota allows 5) maintain public status.

oncall_ava: opened ticket INC-2026-1811 and cloud case: cloud support case id CS-88733. requested emergency quota bump x10. Also manually started a limited scale on dedicated-pool-3: `provisioner resize --pool dedicated-pool-3 --add 4` -> returned `accepted` but will take ~4m to attach.

infra-maya: note: provisioner metrics show call to cloud createInstances has 429 spikes. I'll throttle our provisioner retries to backoff harder to avoid amplifying the cloud rate-limit. change in flight.

runtime-igor: we also saw a bad interaction where the autoscaler attempted to create many small instances instead of a few larger ones -> patching a heuristic to prefer fewer larger instances during global spikes (hotfix queued).

product-sam: can we prepare a customer-facing blurb: short description + mitigation + ETA? keep simple.

support-jade: drafting: "We are experiencing elevated latency and timeouts for some hosted API requests due to GPU provisioning constraints. We have applied traffic routing for impacted customers, enabled temporary throttles, and started CPU fallback nodes. Full recovery depends on cloud quota provisioning; next update in 30 minutes."

oncall_ava: status update (02:10 UTC): cpu-fallback nodes reported ready, router rule active, EastCorp fully routed -> they report 95% success on a sample. global queue depth falling from 12k -> 4.2k. p95 now ~800ms, p99 ~4.2s.

sre-liam: lowering severity to moderate but keep incident channel open. continue monitoring quotas and provisioner.

infra-maya: cloud support replied: temporary +5 g4dn quota in us-east-1 approved, eu-west-1 remains pending. planning to add +3 GPUs to dedicated-pool-3 now.

oncall_ava: applied add +3 -> pool shows +3 attached, token capacity +480. queue down to 2.1k. 504s dropping.

cs-eastcorp: EastCorp confirms degradation nearly resolved; they will keep us posted if any regression. thank you.

product-sam: good job. follow-ups: - postmortem to cover why provisioner retried aggressively and created many small instances - add guardrail to prefer local region capacity before trying cross-region cheap spots - improve autoscaler quota-awareness and a graceful fallback path that avoids saturating provisioner loops.

oncall_ava: created follow-up ticket POSTMORTEM-1811112223 and a runbook todo. closing incident channel in 30m if stable.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity -> moderate. mitigation active. next automated update in 30m.

support-jade: leaving a note for customers: "We’re continuing to monitor; if you still see timeouts, please open an urgent support ticket and include request ids." :white_check_mark:

sre-liam: logging final metrics snapshot to incident ticket: queue_peak=12,043, peak_p99=18.2s, duration_high=22m, cpu_fallback_nodes=8, dedicated_added=+7, cloud_quota_request=CS-88733.

oncall_ava: handoff to daytime oncall @sre-liam in 30 minutes.

support-jade: thanks everyone, nice coordinated effort.
